JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death caused in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioners in the nutshell is that, after finishing of work on 03.10.2022 at about 6.30 p.m, when the deceased was riding the bicycle and in order to filling air to the Tyre he crossing the road on Kanakapura - Malavalli road, Kanakapura town by observing all the traffic rules at that time the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 09-HP-9505 came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and dashed to the deceased bicycle.
Due to the impact the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over his body.

Immediately after the accident he was shifted to Malavalli Government Hospital, wherein he took first aid treatment and then he was shifted to NIMHANS Hospital and then to Victoria Hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and he could not recovered.
Further the treated doctors discharged from hospital and advised to took treatment at nearest hospital.
Further he took treatment at his house and he breathed his last on 17.10.2022.
PM was conducted at Malavalli Government Hospital.
The respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer of the offending scooter.
The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending scooter and as such, the respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Contending the above facts, they pray to grant for compensation with interest and cost.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.1.
Respondent No.1 appeared through his counsel by filing written statement rather objections to the main petition contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.
This respondent has denied that the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car.
The respondent No1 admitted that he is the RC owner of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-09-HP-9505 and was duly insured with the 2nd respondent and same was in force as on the date of accident.
The respondent No.1 denied the rash and negligent riding of the vehicle by its rider but contended that the accident happened because of negligent act of the deceased himself.
It is further submitted that the rider of motorcycle also possess valid and effective driving licence.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.
4. The respondent No.2 appeared through his counsel and filed written statement by contending that the petition is not maintainable either law or on facts.

The respondent No.2 admitting the Nagamma vs Shashank P. Aras on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138774450/
2 issuance of insurance policy in respect of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-09-HP-9505.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.
This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
Negligence on the part of the rider of its insured vehicle is denied by this respondent.
Per contra it is alleged that the accident was occurred due to negligence on the part of the deceased as he was proceeding on the road without observing the traffic rules and regulations.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the rider of the insured vehicle did not possess valid & effective DL as on the date of accident.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a rider.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Non - compliance of section's 134(c), 156(6), 147, 150(2) of MV Act is pleaded.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.
5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that they are only legal representatives of deceased 'Sri. Thimmegowda' and were dependent on him ?

2) Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 03.10.2022 at about 6.30 p.m.,
near Tollgate, Malavalli - Kanakapura road, Malavalli town, Mandya District, due to actionable negligence of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-09-HP-9505 ?

3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation ? If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
4) What order or award ?
6.
Petitioner No.1 examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's.P1 to 20 were marked on behalf of the petitioners.
In order to prove the defence, the respondent No.2 got examined FDA of Malavalli Government Hospital as RW.1 and through him Ex.R.1 & 2 were got marked.
Further the respondent No.1 who is the owner/rider of the offending motorcycle and got examined himself as RW.2.
Ex.R.3 to 6 were got marked through him.
7. Heard erudite counsel for the petitioners and respondents counsel on merits.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

8. This tribunal answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Nagamma vs Shashank P. Aras on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138774450/
3
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.4 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.1 : The petitioners claim that, petitioner No.1 to 3 are the wife, son and married daughter of the deceased.
To prove the same, petitioner No.1 filed affidavit- in-lieu of his chief-examination and deposed about the above relationship.
The PAN cards and Aadhar cards marked at Ex's.P.10 to 15 and contents of the police papers do fortify the said fact.
10. The seminal question to be consider is whether the petitioners No.2 & 3 being the major son and married daughter are the dependents of the deceased.
There is no qualm in the legal preposition of law that the children of the deceased will be the legal representatives.
The moot question to be considered is whether the petitioner No.2 and 3 herein are the dependents of the deceased.

Learned counsel for the respondent No.2 argued in vehemance had contended that the major son and married daughter are not all depending on the income of the deceased, as such compensation cannot be awarded under the head of loss of dependency.
In order to contravert the said contention it is stoutly urged by the learned counsel for the petitioners that even the major son and married daughter are also the dependents.
As such, this Issue and the loss of dependency forms the part of the same transaction the discussion in that regard is also taken under this issue.

entities.text: 2020 (11) SCC 356, (National Insurance Company Limited v. Birender)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The major married son who is also earning and not fully dependent on the deceased would be still covered by the expression "legal representative" of the deceased.

This Court in Manjuri Bera (supra)
had expounded that liability to pay compensation under the Act does not cease because of absence of dependency of the concerned legal representative.
Notably, the expression "legal representative" has not been defined in the Act.
14. It is thus settled by now that the legal representatives of the deceased have a right to apply for compensation.

Having said that, it must necessarily follow that even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only.

The evidence on record in the present case would suggest that the claimants were working as agricultural labourers on contract basis and were earning meager income between Rs. 1,00,000/and Rs. 1,50,000/per annum.

In that sense, they were largely dependent on the earning of their mother and Nagamma vs Shashank P. Aras on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138774450/
4 in fact, were staying with her, who met with an accident at the young age of 48 years."
On the same point of law it is also rely on a decision of Hon'ble High Court of Kerala reported in 2021 SCC Online Kerala 3209 (United India Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Shalumol and Others).

entities.text: 2021 SCC Online Kerala 3209 (United India Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Shalumol and Others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble High Court of Kerala has held in this case, the earning sons are also dependents and also entitled compensation under the Motor Vehicles Act.

11. Further with regard to the married daughters right of claiming compensation it is relevant to relied on a decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in AIR 2007 SC 1474 in the case of Manjura Beri V. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. Wherein it was held that even a married daughter can seek compensation.

entities.text: Manjura Beri V. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the same point of law.

The petitioner has also relied on decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru in MFA No.2332/2013(MV-D) in the case of Dr. Amrutha @
Amruthavathi V/s Chavalla Kumar Raja Naidu & another.
12.

entities.text:
Dr. Amrutha @
Amruthavathi V/s Chavalla Kumar Raja Naidu & another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, in view of the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, which is referred in the above decision, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, the major married / earning sons and married daughters are also dependents to the deceased and they are entitled for the compensation under the motor vehicles accident cases.
It is pertinent to note that, this relationship of the petitioners with the deceased was not disputed by the respondents.

Since the evidence led by the petitioners is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this Tribunal hold that the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased.
Therefore, petitioners are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased.
Hence, this Tribunal answers to issue No.1 In the Affirmative.
13. ISSUE NO.2 :
The petitioners have knocked the doors of justice with a relief to grant a compensation of an amount to the tune of Rs.25,00,000/- together.

The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of complaint lodged by one Sri. Chikkathammaiah herein, the jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed charge sheet against the rider of the Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 09-HP-9505 for the offences punishable under section's 279, 304(A) of IPC.
14.
The respondent No.2 contended that, the offending motorcycle is falsely implicated in this case so as to wangle the compensation amount.
The whole defence of the respondent No.2 is that the insured vehicle was not at all involved in the accident and the deceased himself was responsible fore the accident.
In order to prove the said defence the respondent No.2 examined the FDA of Malavalli Government Hospital as RW.1.
He has produced Authorization letter and MLC extract which are marked as Ex.R.1 & 2.
Petitioners counsel has not cross-examined him.
On perusal of MLC Register extract reveals that the accident is reported and intimated to the jurisdictional police.
Therefore, the defence of the respondent No.2 holds no water.

15. On perusal of spot Mahazar and sketch which are marked as Ex.P.4 & 5 it reflects that, the accident happened on towards Malavalli road situated on Kanakapura - Malavalli road, near Toll,
Malavalli Town, Mandya.
The total width of the road is 32 feets.
It is relevant to note that, accident happened in the city limits.

On conspectus perusal of Ex.P.4 spot mahazar coupled with Ex.P.5 Spot sketch it reflects that the deceased was crossing the road in city limits from Street road towards Nagamma vs Shashank P. Aras on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138774450/
5 Kanakapura road, at that time the rider of motorcycle came from Kanakapura side to proceed towards Malavalli road in a rash and negligent manner and hit the bicycle of the deceased.
Further more Ex.P.4 & 5 documents is supported by Ex.P8 IMV report.
On close perusal it reflects that the front registration number plate, head light, left crush guard, and foot rest of the motorcycle was damaged.
When such being the case, if the motorcycle was driven in a slow speed, he would have definitely avoided the accident.
Added more Ex.P.8 also discloses that the accident was not because of any mechanical defects as such this court does not find any reason to distrust Ex.P.4 & 5 documents.

Further more even a charge sheet was also filed as against the rider of motorcycle as per Ex.P.9.
16.
Another important aspect to be noted here is the evidence of RW.2 who is none other than the owner and rider of the offending vehicle.
RW.2 was himself examined and got marked Ex.R.3 to Ex.R.6.
It is relevant to note that charge sheet is not a sole document on which the factum of negligence has to be decided.

In the instant case on hand, having regard to the other circumstances and other documentary proof it is crystal clear that there was absolutely no negligence on the part of the rider of the bicycle/deceased.
Even in the instant case the IO, as already observed, has clearly opined that the accident occurred only due to the fault of the rider of the motorcycle and he was charge sheeted.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
Though the respondent No.2 has denied the cause of the accident, it has not let in any cogent evidence to prove its defence or to disprove the evidence led by the petitioners.
Therefore, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently, I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 09-HP-9505.
With this observation issue No.2 is answered as 'In the Affirmative.
17. ISSUE NO.3:
In this case the petitioners have claimed the compensation of Rs.25 lakhs on the death of deceased in the road traffic accident.
The petitioners contended that, deceased was doing coolie / Mason and earning of Rs.1,000/- per day.
To prove the income of the deceased, the petitioners have not produced any documents.
Be that as it may, in the absence of authentic proof of income of the deceased, this Tribunal has to consider his income notionally for calculating the compensation.
Admittedly the accident took place in the year 2022.
It is trite law that, when the petitioners have failed to prove the income, the income of the deceased has to be taken into consideration as notional income.
It is relevant to rely on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV) dated.05.07.2023.

entities.text: Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under :
"(b) The accident is of the year 2017.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of Nagamma vs Shashank P. Aras on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138774450/
6 the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
As such this court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred on 03.10.2022.
Therefore, Rs.15,500/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the deceased.

18. So far as the age of the deceased is concerned, the petitioners have produced the Aadhar card to show the age of the deceased as per Ex.P16 wherein the date of birth of deceased is shown as 01.01.1961, which indicates that he was aged 61 years 9 months 2 days days on the date of accident.
During the course of cross examination of PW.1 also admitted that on the day of accident the deceased is aged 62 years.

Therefore the appropriate multiplier as per Sarla Verma's case for the said age group is '7'.
19.
In the case on hand the deceased was aged 62 years.
His income is taken as Rs.15,500/- p.m.
As per dictum of Hon'ble Apex Court in AIR 2017 SC 5157, the deceased is not entitled to future prospects (as he was aged more than 60 years).
The deceased died living behind 3 dependents.

As per principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarala Verma Case, 1/3rd of his income is required to be deducted towards his personal expenses which comes to Rs.10,333/- p.m. (Rs.15,500 - Rs.5,167 = Rs.10,333/-).
20. The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.10,333/- p.m. and the multiplier '7' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.8,67,972/- (Rs.10,333 X 12 X 7).
Considering the above facts, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.8,68,000/- under the head of loss of dependency.

21. Further, as Law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to estate, funeral expenses and consortium is to be awarded.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners contended that they have spent substantial amount towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies etc., but no documents are produced.
Hence this Tribunal award Rs.18,150/- towards loss to estate and Rs.18,150/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years.

Rs.48,400/- towards consortium to the petitioner No.1 by applying the observations made in the aforesaid case, as more than 6 years elapsed from the date of order amount of consortium, funeral expense and loss of estate to be enhanced.

22. In this case, the petitioner No.2 & 3 are the children of the deceased and as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioner No.2 & 3 are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an accidental death of a children and father as the case may be.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An accident leading to the death of a mother cause great shock and agony to the children of the deceased and they lost their love and affection towards his/her mother.

Therefore, petitioner No.2 & 3 are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each Nagamma vs Shashank P. Aras on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138774450/
7 under the head of Filial consortium.
23. MEDICAL EXPENSES : 7-Medical bills produced by PW.1 are marked at Ex.P19.
As per that, the claimants have spent Rs.3,175/- towards medical expenses of the deceased.
The said bills have been meticulously examined and is found to be correct.
There is no contra evidence to disbelieve the genuineness of these bills.
Hence a sum of Rs.3,175/- which is rounded off to Rs.3,200/- is awarded under this head.

24. The calculation table stands as follows :
Compensation heads Compensation amount 1.
Towards loss of dependency Rs. 8,68,000/-
2. Towards loss of Consortium to Rs. 48,400/- the petitioner No.1 3.
Towards loss to estate Rs. 18,150/-

4. Towards transportation of dead Rs. 18,150/-
body funeral and obsequies ceremony expenses 5.

Towards loss of Filial Rs. 80,000/-
6. Medical Expenses Rs. 3,200/-
Total Rs.10,35,900/-
25.

REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY: Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
26. The issuance of policy in respect of the offending vehicle and the fact that it was in force at the time of accident is admitted by the 2 nd respondent / Insurance Company.
The accident was occurred on the negligence of the driver of the offending motorcycle.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-09-HP-9505 are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However, the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Hence issue No.3 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
27. ISSUE NO.4 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :

8 ORDER

The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.10,35,900/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
 Petitioner No.1 - 80%
 Petitioner No.2 - 10%
 Petitioner No.3 - 10%
Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 a sum equal to 25% shall be deposited in her name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of her choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 75% shall be released to her through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on her deposit amount from time to time.
After deposit of compensation amount the office is directed to release the entire share with interest of the petitioner No.2 & 3 through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.

ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that they are only legal representatives of deceased 'Sri. Thimmegowda' and were dependent on him ?
2) Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 03.10.2022 at about 6.30 p.m.,
near Tollgate, Malavalli - Kanakapura road, Malavalli town, Mandya District, due to actionable negligence of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-09-HP-9505 ?
3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation ? If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
4) What order or award ?

10. The seminal question to be consider is whether the petitioners No.2 & 3 being the major son and married daughter are the dependents of the deceased.
The moot question to be considered is whether the petitioner No.2 and 3 herein are the dependents of the deceased.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
On the same point of law it is also rely on a decision of Hon'ble High Court of Kerala reported in 2021 SCC Online Kerala 3209 (United India Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Shalumol and Others).
Therefore, in view of the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, which is referred in the above decision, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, the major married / earning sons and married daughters are also dependents to the deceased and they are entitled for the compensation under the motor vehicles accident cases.
Therefore, petitioners are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased.
The respondent No.2 contended that, the offending motorcycle is falsely implicated in this case so as to wangle the compensation amount.
The whole defence of the respondent No.2 is that the insured vehicle was not at all involved in the accident and the deceased himself was responsible fore the accident.
In the instant case on hand, having regard to the other circumstances and other documentary proof it is crystal clear that there was absolutely no negligence on the part of the rider of the bicycle/deceased.
Even in the instant case the IO, as already observed, has clearly opined that the accident occurred only due to the fault of the rider of the motorcycle and he was charge sheeted.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
The petitioners contended that, deceased was doing coolie / Mason and earning of Rs.1,000/- per day.
To prove the income of the deceased, the petitioners have not produced any documents.
Be that as it may, in the absence of authentic proof of income of the deceased, this Tribunal has to consider his income notionally for calculating the compensation.
Admittedly the accident took place in the year 2022.
It is trite law that, when the petitioners have failed to prove the income, the income of the deceased has to be taken into consideration as notional income.
The deceased died living behind 3 dependents.

In this case, the petitioner No.2 & 3 are the children of the deceased and as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioner No.2 & 3 are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an accidental death of a children and father as the case may be.
26. The issuance of policy in respect of the offending vehicle and the fact that it was in force at the time of accident is admitted by the 2 nd respondent / Insurance Company.
The accident was occurred on the negligence of the driver of the offending motorcycle.
However, the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Considering the above facts, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.8,68,000/- under the head of loss of dependency.
Hence this Tribunal award Rs.18,150/- towards loss to estate and Rs.18,150/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years.
Rs.48,400/- towards consortium to the petitioner No.1 by applying the observations made in the aforesaid case, as more than 6 years elapsed from the date of order amount of consortium, funeral expense and loss of estate to be enhanced.

Hence issue No.3 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.

8 ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.10,35,900/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
 Petitioner No.1 - 80%
 Petitioner No.2 - 10%
 Petitioner No.3 - 10%
Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 a sum equal to 25% shall be deposited in her name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of her choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 75% shall be released to her through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on her deposit amount from time to time.
After deposit of compensation amount the office is directed to release the entire share with interest of the petitioner No.2 & 3 through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
